summary: The lecture covers Environment and Ecology Part 3, focusing on Ecotone and Edge Effect definitions, Ecological Niche and Competitive Exclusion Principle, Biome classification, Ecological Succession stages (Primary/Secondary), Wetland types and Ramsar Convention details (80 Indian sites, Montreux Record), Mangrove adaptations (vivipary, pneumatophores), Coral Reef symbiosis and reef types, and Productivity concepts (GPP, NPP) with Green Carbon storage in peatlands.
points: Ecotone: Transition zone between two ecosystems (e.g., estuaries, mangroves); exhibits Edge Effect and higher species diversity (Edge Species).
Edge Effect: Changes in community structure at habitat boundary; natural (river-ocean) or artificial (road in forest).
Ecological Niche: Unique functional role of species (habitat, food, reproduction); Competitive Exclusion Principle: two species cannot occupy same niche.
Biome: Large climatic region (temperature/moisture) comprising multiple ecosystems; classified via Whittaker diagram.
Ecological Succession: Primary (bare rock, slow, pioneers: lichens/mosses) vs Secondary (disturbed soil, faster); ends in Climax community.
Wetlands: Ecotone land-water, depth ≤6m; Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran) promotes wise use; World Wetlands Day: Feb 2.
India has 80 Ramsar sites (2024); Montreux Record lists degraded wetlands (Chilika, Loktak); Wetland Rules 2017 delegate identification to States.
Mangroves: Salt-tolerant coastal trees in tropical intertidal zones; Vivipary reproduction; adaptations: pneumatophores, prop roots, salt excretion.
Coral Reefs: Symbiosis of polyps & zooxanthellae; Hard corals build reefs (tropical, 20-27°C, <55m); Types: Fringing, Barrier, Atoll.
Productivity: GPP = total photosynthetic biomass; NPP = GPP - Respiration; Highest GPP in wetlands/estuaries. Peatlands (Congo Basin) store max Green Carbon.
